create.name: Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago
create.bio:
Founded in January 1930 by Swami Jnaneswarananda, the Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago belongs to the Ramakrishna Order and grew up in the city where Swami Vivekananda spoke at the 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions. Over the decades it moved from rented rooms downtown to Hyde Park, and since 2008 its main temple and monastery have stood in Homer Glen, south-west of Chicago. Swami Bhashyananda, who led it from the 1960s, opened the Vivekananda Retreat at Ganges, Michigan, in 1971, and the society now also runs the Home of Harmony on the city's north side. Swami Ishatmananda has been minister in charge since 2013.

Its teaching follows Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi and Vivekananda: one reality behind all things, the divinity of each person and respect for every faith. At Homer Glen there is daily worship and vespers, a Sunday talk and a Wednesday class on Ramakrishna's life, much of it streamed. The Ganges retreat offers quiet days of prayer and study, a shrine trail and summer weekend retreats, while the Home of Harmony hosts interfaith talks, free yoga and meditation sessions and the School of World Religions, a set of no-cost online courses. Its YouTube channel holds well over a thousand recorded talks and scripture classes.

free_resources.title: School of World Religions (online courses)
free_resources.description: Self-paced online courses run by the society's Home of Harmony, including a systematic study of Hinduism and introductions to Buddhism, the Abrahamic faiths and Zoroastrianism. Enrolment is free, with donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Sunday Talks, Classes and Programmes
free_resources.description: The monthly schedule for the Homer Glen temple and the Home of Harmony: Sunday talks, the online Wednesday class on Ramakrishna's life, Ram Nam chanting and Saturday interfaith talks.

free_resources.title: Vivekananda Retreat, Ganges
free_resources.description: The society's retreat in rural Michigan, with morning prayer and evening vespers each day, a library, a small museum and a mile-long trail of shrines to the world's religions. Seekers may come for quiet days of prayer, meditation and study.

free_resources.title: Home of Harmony
free_resources.description: An interfaith centre on Chicago's north side with free Saturday talks and concerts, weekly Sunday yoga and meditation open to walk-ins, and a reading room.
